result.output: # Frame Job [![Frame Job in 90 seconds: watch on YouTube](https://img.youtube.com/vi/An7KjPoofzI/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_xkkMhgNRQU) A native macOS video editor. Open a movie, arrange it on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, then trim, cut, grade, caption, animate and export it. Every edit you make in the window can also be made by an AI agent over MCP, or by the built-in Assistant, and each one is an ordinary undo step. Apple Silicon, macOS 26 or later. There is no account to make: every AI feature runs on your own API key (Anthropic for the Assistant, AssemblyAI for cloud transcription), and everything else works without one. ## Open a movie and start cutting **File ▸ Open…** (⌘O) on a `.mov` or `.mp4` — or a drop on the Dock icon, or **Open Video…** in the Welcome window — creates an *untitled* project sized and rated to that file, with the file as the first clip on Track 1, ready to cut. A portrait phone clip opens portrait, and a 29.97 fps file stays 29.97. **Save** then writes a `.framejob` package, offered next to the source. ## Features **Projects and media.** Movies, sound and pictures from everything macOS plays, plus WebM and MKV copied in without re-encoding; missing files relinked; Consolidate Media copies footage into the package. → [Projects and media](docs/site/src/content/docs/projects/start-a-project.mdx) **Timeline.** One kind of track that holds any clip; a frame-accurate ruler, filmstrips and waveforms, zoom about the cursor, snapping, markers, an in/out range, track mute, solo, lock, volume, pan, compressor and limiter, clip names and colour labels. → [The timeline and playback](docs/site/src/content/docs/timeline/tracks.mdx) **Editing.** Move, nudge, trim, slip, roll, split, lift, ripple delete, close gap, insert time, insert and overwrite, copy and paste, Paste Attributes, and nests that group clips into one. → [Editing clips](docs/site/src/content/docs/editing/how-edits-work.mdx) **Canvas and layers.** Move, scale, rotate and crop on the preview; opacity, blend modes, shadows, filters, chroma key, spotlight and obscure; Remove Background, which keeps the person (or a photo's subject) and drops the rest with no green screen, found on your Mac, and Text Behind Subject, a title the person stands in front of; text, shape, image and background clips; matte tracks that cut the track behind them. → [Canvas, layers, text and shapes](docs/site/src/content/docs/canvas/the-canvas.mdx) **Vertical and framing.** Faces, people and the regions the eye goes to, found on your Mac and drawn over the preview by View ▸ Show Subjects; Clip ▸ Follow Subject… frames landscape recordings for a vertical or square canvas, easing onto the subject, cutting with the shots and filling the edges with a blurred copy, as ordinary actions in one undo step. File ▸ Make Vertical Version… turns a whole landscape edit into its 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1 version in a new project, each full-frame shot following its subject — or, for a wide shot of two to four people with a microphone each, whoever is talking — and titles and pictures-in-picture kept as placed. → [Vertical and framing](docs/site/src/content/docs/framing/what-is-found.mdx) **Motion and transitions.** Actions that ease any property to a new state over a span — Zoom to Region for screencasts — motion presets for entrances, exits and continuous movement, and thirteen transition styles. → [Motion, actions and transitions](docs/site/src/content/docs/motion/actions.mdx) **Speed.** Constant speed or fit to a length, ⌥-drag rate stretch, keep pitch, reverse, freeze frame, and speed ramps — **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** makes a Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Speed Dip or Speed Burst in one step. → [Speed, reverse and freeze frames](docs/site/src/content/docs/speed/overview.mdx) **Audio.** Per-clip volume, drawn as a line on each clip that you drag and ⌥-click to add points, fades in four shapes, ducking for a clip's length or only while its speech plays, voice isolation (Apple's on-device voice model, which also reduces room echo), sixteen voice effects (pitch, robot, telephone, radio, echo, reverbs and more), channel selection, EQ with voice presets, hum removal, noise reduction, a gate for the pauses, a leveller that evens out a speaker who moves on and off the mic, phrase by phrase, and a de-esser, each set from the clip's own loudness, compressor, pan, mono and a true-peak limiter, each of them animated by actions as the volume is; each clip's loudness and true peak in the inspector; Enhance Voice, which sets a voice recording up for speech from its own measurements in one step; Match Audio, which gives clips another clip's loudness and speech tone; and Normalize to a loudness target (−16 LUFS at −1 dBTP by default, turning the limiter on when a clip's peaks need it) or to a peak, which matches clips; a live loudness meter for the mix as it plays; Synchronize Audio lines up a camera and a separate recorder by their sound, drift included. Detach Audio keeps the sound linked to its picture, so J- and L-cuts stay in sync through every edit, and Attach Audio puts it back. → [Audio](docs/site/src/content/docs/audio/how-audio-works.mdx) **Clean-up tools.** Remove Silences cuts dead air by voice or by level; Remove Filler Words cuts the ums and uhs on their own timings. Both preview the cuts and make them as one undo step. → [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](docs/site/src/content/docs/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work.mdx) **Captions.** Import and export SubRip or WebVTT; generate captions on this Mac or with AssemblyAI, as two-line subtitles or word-by-word captions in five styles. Every caption is an ordinary text clip. → [Captions and transcription](docs/site/src/content/docs/captions/how-captions-work.mdx) **Colour grading.** Light and colour controls, three wheels, curves, eight built-in looks and your own `.cube` LUTs, adjustment clips with qualifiers, Show Ungraded, and waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram scopes. → [Colour grading](docs/site/src/content/docs/color/color-tab.mdx) **HDR and colour management.** iPhone HDR, HDR10, wide gamut and camera log read as what they are; SDR or HDR (HLG) projects; HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables, with Show SDR Version to preview the last. → [HDR and colour management](docs/site/src/content/docs/hdr/how-sources-are-read.mdx) **Motion graphics.** Graphic clips drawn every frame by a small JavaScript module: 23 built-ins, browsed by category with a live looping preview in the Graphic dialog: charts, a gauge and timers, screencast keys and window frames, title, quote and logo cards, and social pop-ups; properties as inspector controls, your own modules too, each saved to share as a `.fjgraphic` file with only the fonts and pictures it uses, which Frame Job opens to import into a project. → [Motion graphics](docs/site/src/content/docs/graphics/what-is-a-graphic.mdx) **Several cameras.** Each camera on a track of its own and a program track cut from them; **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** cuts that program from the microphones, showing whoever is talking and the wide while both talk, and **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸** re-picks a shot from another camera in sync, keeping its span and its dissolves, each in one undo step. → [Podcasts and several cameras](docs/site/src/content/docs/multicam/set-up.mdx) **Screen recording.** A display or a window, with system audio, microphone and click rings, at 30 or 60 fps, into a new project or at the playhead; a camera, on its own or beside the screen as a corner talking head; or a microphone-only voice-over. A screen recording's cursor is recorded separately and drawn by Frame Job, so you can resize, smooth or hide it after the fact. **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** zooms a recording in at its clicks and typing and back out after, as ordinary actions you can edit, and **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays** shows the shortcuts you pressed as keycaps. **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** plays the typing faster where nobody speaks. → [Screen recording](docs/site/src/content/docs/recording/recorder-panel.mdx) **Export.** H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), AV1 in MP4 or WebM (10-bit, with HDR, from its own encoder built in, at three speeds; Opus sound in the WebM), VP9 in WebM for every browser (8-bit, or 10-bit with HDR, also built in, with Opus) and with alpha for transparent web video, ProRes 422 and 4444, M4A, WAV and AIFF (16- or 24-bit, with stems: a file per track beside the mix), GIF and animated PNG; loudness targets reached through a true-peak master limiter on every export, presets, an Export Queue that runs while you edit, and single frames as stills. → [Exporting](docs/site/src/content/docs/export/export-sheet.mdx) **The Assistant.** A conversation with Claude in the inspector that edits the open project with the same tools an agent uses, asks before it saves or exports, and shows what each turn cost. → [The Assistant](docs/site/src/content/docs/assistant/set-up.mdx) **The Transcript.** Everything said on the timeline as text in the inspector, in paragraphs with timecodes, read on this Mac or from an AssemblyAI transcript; the spoken word lights up and the text follows it as the video plays, and a click on a word moves the playhead there. title: AI features and your own keys
description: Which features need nothing, which use an on-device model, which need your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, and what ever leaves your Mac.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Most of Frame Job needs no key and no network. The few features that send your words or audio to a cloud model run on your own API keys, so you decide what's used and you pay the provider directly.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where={['Settings ▸ Assistant', 'Settings ▸ Transcription']}
  tools={['transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers']}
  needs="Your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, only for the features that send to them."
/>

## Your own keys

There's no Frame Job account and no relay in between. There are two keys in all, and each provider bills your account directly.

| Key | Turns on | Saved in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic | The Assistant | [Settings ▸ Assistant](/assistant/set-up/) |
| AssemblyAI | Cloud captions and Remove Filler Words | [Settings ▸ Transcription](/captions/assemblyai-key/) |

Frame Job shows its own estimate of what each Assistant turn and each month costs. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). The provider's bill is the real figure.

With no key set, Settings says "No API key is set." in its ordinary muted colour. That only means there's no key yet, and it isn't an error.

## What needs what

Anything that sends your words or audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.

| What it takes | Features |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing | Editing, colour, graphics, recording, export, Split at Shot Changes, and connecting an [MCP client](/mcp/overview/#an-mcp-client-or-the-assistant), which brings its own model |
| An on-device model, with no key and no upload | **Generate Captions** with **On this Mac**, Remove Silences' voice analysis, Enhance Voice and Voice Isolation, Remove Background, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and Switch by Speaker |
| Your AssemblyAI key | The **AssemblyAI** engine of **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, and **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** with its **Transcribe** buttons |
| Your Anthropic key | The Assistant |

Filler removal works only through AssemblyAI. There's no on-device version.

Without your Anthropic key, **View ▸ Assistant** still opens the tab, which says how to add the key.

Work you've already paid for keeps working with no key:

- **Generate** isn't greyed when every file is already transcribed.
- **Remove Filler Words…** stays on while a file it would work on has a current transcript made with filler words.

An on-device language that isn't installed yet shows a **Download** row in the [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) sheet.

## Greyed commands

A command that needs a key you haven't set is greyed rather than hidden, and it says which key and where to set it.

A greyed menu item's title gains the key's name, as in **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. Rest the pointer on a greyed command or button and it reads:

> No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.

For the Assistant it's the same sentence with Anthropic and Assistant. The Assistant tab itself reads "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." with an **Open Settings…** button.

An agent's tool stops with the same sentence, at the point it would send. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) for what still works without a key.

## Saving a key takes effect at once

Saving or removing a key updates open sheets and menu items straight away. An open Generate Captions sheet turns **Generate** back on with the sheet still up, and there's nothing to reopen or relaunch.

## What stays on this Mac

Editing, analysis, on-device transcription, recording and export all stay on this Mac. Only these reach the network, and each is something you start or can see:

| Goes to | What | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AssemblyAI | The audio of the files being transcribed | When you press **Generate** or **Transcribe** with that engine. **Verify** in Settings also makes a small request with your key, with no audio. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/). |
| Anthropic | Your Assistant messages, the project's details and the frames it renders | While you use the Assistant. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/). |
| GitHub | A request for LiteLLM's published price table, which the cost estimates use, with no key and no project data | At most once a day, from the Assistant's helper |
| GitHub | A check of the update feed, and the update itself when you choose to install one | In the [downloaded copy](/getting-started/updates/) only, when you check or if you allowed automatic checks |
| macOS's own download | An on-device speech model | When you ask for one |

# Frame Job

**A native macOS video editor. Cut it yourself, ask the Assistant, or let any MCP agent drive.**

## In one line

Frame Job is a free, open-source video editor for the Mac, which you, its built-in Assistant or any AI agent can edit with.

## In a paragraph

Frame Job is a native macOS video editor. Open a movie, arrange it on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, then trim, cut, grade, caption, animate and export it. It's built for spoken video: you can cut by deleting words from the transcript, take out silences and filler words, record your screen and camera, and turn a landscape edit into a vertical one. Every edit you make in the window can also be made by the built-in Assistant or by an AI agent over MCP, and each one is an ordinary undo step. It's free, open source under the Apache 2.0 licence, and there's no account to make.

---

## What Frame Job is

Frame Job is a video editor written for the Mac from the ground up. The interface is Swift and AppKit, playback and export use Apple's own video frameworks, and the compositing runs on the GPU through Metal. The editing model, every edit and the timeline itself live in a Rust core.

It's for people who make video with a person talking in it: screencasts and tutorials, podcasts, interviews and talking-head clips for social media. It's also a complete general editor, with layered tracks, colour grading, motion graphics and HDR.

## What you can do with it

- **Start in seconds.** Open a `.mov` or `.mp4` and Frame Job makes a project sized and timed to it, with the file already on the timeline. A portrait phone clip opens portrait, and a 29.97 fps file stays 29.97.
- **Edit on tracks that hold anything.** Trim, slip, roll, split, ripple delete, insert and overwrite, and group clips into nests. The timeline has filmstrips and waveforms, snapping, markers, and track mute, solo and lock.
- **Compose on a canvas.** Move, scale, rotate and crop on the preview. Add text, shapes and pictures, blend modes, shadows and chroma key, and use matte tracks to cut one layer with another. Remove Background keeps the person and drops the rest, with no green screen.
- **Animate.** Ease any property to a new state over a span of time, use Zoom to Region for screencasts, pick from motion presets for entrances and exits, and choose from thirteen transition styles.
- **Change speed.** Constant speed or fit to a length, keep pitch, reverse, freeze frames, and speed ramps made in one step.
- **Make the sound right.** Volume lines and fades, ducking under speech, voice isolation, EQ, hum and noise removal, a leveller, a de-esser, compressor and limiter, and sixteen voice effects. Enhance Voice sets a voice recording up in one step, Normalize brings clips to a loudness target, and Synchronize Audio lines a camera up with a separate recorder by their sound.
- **Grade.** Light and colour controls, three wheels, curves, built-in looks and your own `.cube` LUTs, adjustment clips with qualifiers, and waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram scopes.
- **Work in HDR.** iPhone HDR, HDR10, wide gamut and camera log are read as what they are. Make SDR or HDR projects, and deliver HLG, HDR10 and an SDR version.
- **Add motion graphics.** 23 built-in graphics, including charts, timers, keyboard keys for screencasts, title and quote cards and social pop-ups, each with its own controls. Write your own in JavaScript and share them as a single file.
- **Export.** H.264, HEVC (including 10-bit and transparent video), AV1 and VP9 for the web, ProRes, audio-only files with a separate file per track, GIF and animated PNG. Every export meets its loudness target, and the Export Queue runs while you keep editing.

## Made for spoken video

- **Edit the transcript.** Everything said on the timeline appears as text, and the spoken word lights up as the video plays. Select words and press Delete to cut them from every track at once.
- **Take out the gaps.** Remove Silences cuts dead air, and Remove Filler Words cuts the ums and uhs. You preview the cuts first, and they land as one undo step.
- **Caption.** Generate captions on your Mac or with AssemblyAI, as two-line subtitles or word-by-word captions in five styles, or import and export SubRip and WebVTT.
- **Record your screen.** Record a display or a window with system audio, your microphone and click rings, with your camera in the corner if you like. The cursor is recorded separately, so you can resize, smooth or hide it afterwards. Auto Zoom zooms in on your clicks and typing, and Speed Up Typing plays the typing faster where nobody speaks.
- **Go vertical.** Follow Subject keeps the person in frame on a vertical or square canvas. Make Vertical Version turns a whole landscape edit into 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1, following whoever is talking in a wide shot of several people.
- **Cut a podcast from several cameras.** Switch by Speaker cuts the program from the microphones, showing whoever is talking and the wide shot while both talk.

## AI, on your terms

Most of Frame Job needs no key and no network. There's no Frame Job account and no service in between.

- **On your Mac.** On-device captions, voice detection for Remove Silences, voice isolation, Remove Background, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and Switch by Speaker all run locally, with no key and no upload.
- **Your own keys.** The two features that send audio or words to a cloud model use your own API keys, and the provider bills you directly: AssemblyAI for cloud captions and filler words, and Anthropic for the Assistant. A feature that needs a key you haven't set says which key and where to set it.
- **The Assistant.** A conversation with Claude in the inspector that edits the open project with the same tools an agent uses. It asks before it saves or exports, and shows what each turn cost.
- **Agents over MCP.** The whole editor is available as MCP tools: one per edit, plus open, save, render a frame and export. Claude Code or any other MCP client can drive it. Settings copies the command that connects Claude Code. The connection is a local socket that only programs on your Mac can open, and Frame Job starts in the background when an agent first needs it.

## Requirements

- A Mac with Apple silicon.
- macOS 26 or later.

## Download

The download is a signed and notarized disk image: [FrameJob.dmg](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/releases/latest/download/FrameJob.dmg). Open it and drag Frame Job to Applications. Frame Job updates itself, through **Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…** or automatic checks if you allow them.

## Open source

Frame Job is free and open source under the Apache License 2.0. The source code, releases and issue tracker are on [GitHub](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob).

=== #535
set_action_end can carry a crop, corner radius or chroma key onto a text, shape or graphic clip
Found while fixing #524 (ai-docs batch b1).

#524 made `set_video` refuse a crop, a corner radius or a chroma key on a text, shape or graphic clip, and made Paste Attributes leave such a clip's own. `switch_layout` now refuses up front when its own layout action would crop or round a shape or graphic clip.

An action's end patch is not covered. `set_action_end` checks the patch's vocabulary (`check_end_patch` in `core/src/edit_action_end.rs`) and never the clip's kind, so a hand-written `set_action_end` with `{"video": {"corner_radius": 40}}` on an action on a shape clip would still write a corner radius that no section shows.

**What was run:** nothing. This was read from the code during the batch. It was not run in the app or in a core test, so it is unverified.

**To decide:** whether `check_end_patch` (or its caller) refuses these keys on a text, shape or graphic clip the way `set_video` now does, or whether `actions_clamp.rs` drops them for these kinds. The answer for #524 was "refuse and skip", which points to a refusal.

=== #536
Nest and adjustment clips take a crop, corner radius or chroma key that no section shows
Found while fixing #524 (ai-docs batch b1).

Nest clips and adjustment clips have no Crop, Corner Radius or Chroma Key section in the inspector (`InspectorTab.hasSourcePixels` answers false for them). Even so, `set_video` and Paste Attributes still write all three keys on them. The answer for #524 covered only text, shape and graphic clips, so the batch left these two kinds as they were.

**What was run:** nothing on these two kinds. This was read from the code during the batch. It was not run in the app, so it is unverified.

**Needs an owner choice:**
- Refuse them as #524 does for text, shape and graphic clips: `set_video` refuses, and Paste Attributes skips.
- Or keep them, as they may draw something on a nest clip's picture, and say so on the docs pages.

=== #537
Pressing play holds the playhead for about half a second before it moves
Found while measuring #520 (ai-docs batch a1). Related to #520, which holds the same way at every Loop wrap and every seek made while playing.

**What happens**

On a timeline whose clip has sound, pressing play from paused holds the player's clock for about half a second before the playhead moves.

**What was run**

The built Debug app over MCP (the frozen base build, main at d40d1f81), on a test project made in it from `tools/proof/media/AV.mov` (5 s, h264 + aac), with the default output on the built-in speakers. `tools/proof/ai_docs_a1_proof.py`'s W4 row: `play_preview` for 4 s from 0, paused, three trials. The start deficit D is the wall time less the distance the player's own `currentTime` moved.

- AV.mov with its sound: D was 0.520, 0.531 and 0.533 s.
- The same clip with its sound off (`set_enabled {audio: false}`, W6), and a movie with no audio stream (W7): D was 0.009 to 0.021 s.
- A spike build with the preview's audio taps off (`metering: false` in `Playback.startRebuild`, measured and not shipped): D was 0.201 to 0.218 s.

So the hold needs sound, and the taps account for part of it but not all.

**Not known**

- The cause beyond the above.
- Whether a person sees a frozen picture or hears a gap at the start; only the player's clock was measured.

=== #538
App strings still mix British and American spelling beyond colour/centre
#526 settled American spelling for the app's own strings (the owner, 2026-11-06: "American ... Color, center, centered and so on"; spec §11 #526) and changed colour and centre (commit 387f9d06 on main, not yet pushed). Other British forms remain in strings a person or a caller reads.

=== #539
Recapture the Qualifier and Document tab inspector screens at 2× (they are 304 × 539)
In ai-docs batch c2 (#526, commit 387f9d06 on main, not yet pushed), two inspector screens were recaptured so they show the American spellings ("Color" on the Document tab, "Center" on the Qualifier). The editor window opened on a 1× display, so the four captures landed at 304 × 539. The previous captures and every sibling inspector shot (for example `05b-clip-color.inspector.light.webp`) are 608 × 1078. `docs/site/src/components/Shot.astro` sets the figure's `max-width` to half the image width, so the Qualifier and Document tab pages now show these shots at 152 px wide, half the size of every other inspector shot.

- `docs/site/src/assets/screens/05h-clip-qualifier.inspector.dark.webp`

=== #540
Turning Remove Background on or off with no action selected can send a whole cutout to a first-frame cut's end, which the core refuses
Found by reading the code in the review of batch ai-docs a2 (#529, #530, commit 3774ccbe on main, not yet pushed). Nothing was run for this: it is a lead, not a measurement.

**What the code does.** Since #530, a video write in the inspector on a clip with a first-frame cut (a camera layout at clip time 0), with no action selected, also sends `set_action_end` to the cut with every key the cut's end already names (`VideoPatch.held(by:)` in `CanvasEditTarget.swift`, called from `keepingCuts` in `InspectorBinding+Writes.swift`). `held(by:)` keeps `cutout` whole whenever the cut's end names `cutout`, which happens once a person has animated Background (the sparse `cutoutPart`) on the cut.

**Why that is wrong.** A cutout's presence is the clip's own (spec §11 CO-20, CO-30 (b)): `set_action_end` refuses a `video.cutout` naming `subject` or `quality`, and a null one (`check_cutout_end` and the `off` rule in `core/src/edit_action_end.rs`). `structural(video:for:)` already keeps a whole or null `cutout` off an end for that reason, and sends only `cutoutPart` there.

**Expected effect (unmeasured).** Animate Background on a recording's camera at its first-frame cut, deselect the action, then turn Remove Background off or on, or press its Reset. The base write applies; the cut's `set_action_end` is refused, so that op is dropped without a word. The same reading may apply to a `filters` or `obscure` list of a different length when the cut's end already names that list, which `structural(video:for:)` sends to the base only.

**Suggested fix.** In `held(by:)`, keep only `cutoutPart` under `cutout` (never a whole or null `cutout`), and run the held patch through the same structural rule an end write uses. Add a row to `tools/proof/docs_bugs_a3_proof.py` that animates Background on the cut, toggles Remove Background with no action selected, and reads back that no op was refused and frame 0 agrees with frame 1.

Confirmed in ai-docs batch a1, measured, not fixed. It stays open.

**What was run:** the built Debug app over MCP (the base build, main at d40d1f81), on test projects made from `AV.mov` (5 s, h264 + aac): one clip with its Loop on (Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview), and two clips with the loop on the first (the loop ending inside the timeline). `play_preview` answers the player's own `currentTime`, so the hold is the wall time the player's clock did not move: one wrap (8 s plays), two wraps (13 s plays), three trials per row, and twice on two separate runs. A second measure polled `get_project` as fast as the socket answers (0.3–1.0 ms apart) for 16 s. `playback_rebuilds` counted rebuilds over the loop runs.

**What it showed:**

- **The player itself holds, not only the report.** Per wrap, the hold was 0.678–0.719 s in every trial, the same on one clip and on two. The fine poll read exactly 0.0 for 0.66–0.68 s at every wrap, then advanced in 1/60 s steps with no jump forward. There were 0 rebuilds.
- **It is every seek while playing, not the loop logic.** With Loop off, a seek in the middle of a play held about 0.55 s.
- **It needs sound.** With the clip's sound off, the wrap hold was about 0.02 s, and with a movie that has no audio stream it was about 0.02 s too.

Two candidate changes were built and measured in Debug, with the built-in speakers, and neither shipped:

| Build | Per-wrap hold, one clip | Two clips | Mid-play seek hold |
|---|---|---|---|
| The base app | 0.695 s | — | 0.552 s |
| A seek made while playing forward does not wait for the compositor's frame (`seekingWaitsForVideoCompositionRendering` false) | 0.657 s | 0.661 s | 0.546 s |
| A preview built with no audio taps (`metering: false`; it would leave the level meter dark) | 0.447 s | 0.277 s (trials 0.277, 0.258, 1.013) | 0.196 s |

So the preview's audio taps account for part of the hold, and something else in the sound path holds the rest. The Release build read the same (a wrap hold of 0.734 s, a seek hold of 0.562 s, with the output on Bluetooth). Whether a person sees a frozen picture or hears a gap was not checked; only the player's clock was measured.

`tools/proof/ai_docs_a1_proof.py`'s W1–W7 rows print these numbers as measurements, not scores, so a later fix can be measured against them. The half-second hold when play starts from paused, which looks related, is filed as #537.

Confirmed in the built app, investigated, and **held for the owner**. No fix shipped, so this stays open.

## What was run

The built app was driven over MCP on a test project made from a 5 s h264 + aac movie.

- **The measurement.** D is the start deficit: the wall time of a 4 s `play_preview` started from paused at 0, minus the distance the player's own clock moved.
- **On the frozen base app**, D was:
  - Loop off, two clips: median 0.533 s.
  - Loop on, one clip: median 0.544 s.
  - Every trial in the confirm stage read 0.519–0.632 s, over three launches, on AirPods Max and on the built-in speakers.
- **The controls held about 0.01–0.04 s:**
  - the same clip with its sound off;
  - a movie with no audio stream.

  So the hold needs sound, and the output device's latency does not explain it.
- **Four candidate changes were each built alone and measured, then reverted** (H1 is Loop off, H2 is Loop on; medians of 3 trials):
  - S1: the ×1 track's time-pitch set to `.varispeed`. H1 0.471 s, H2 0.450 s.
  - S2: the player item's time-pitch set to `.varispeed`, with every track's left unset. H1 0.447 s, H2 0.451 s.
  - S3: the audio taps moved after the effects. H1 0.359 s, H2 0.281 s.
  - S4: prerolling the player at ×1 once a seek lands paused. H1 0.528 s, H2 0.521 s.

  None got under the 0.10 s line, which sits between the controls and round 1's half-fix.

The new proof `tools/proof/ai_docs_r2a_proof.py` prints H1 and H2 as measurements against that line. It scores only the level meter still metering (M1) and the parity log (Z1). It ran whole on the batch's Debug and Release builds:
- Debug: H1 0.532 s, H2 0.534 s.
- Release: H1 0.538 s, H2 0.531 s.
- M1 and Z1 passed on both.

`docs/manual-checks.md` PB-15 names the hold. The proof, its README section and that row are commit 312b0816 on main (not yet pushed).

The same cause holds #520's wrap and mid-play seek, so both are held together.
## Held for the owner: the question

**Where the hold comes from, as far as it was found:**
- About half of it comes from where the processing taps sit, before the effects. S3, which moved them after the effects, brought the start deficit to 0.28–0.36 s, mid-play seeks to 0.21 s and wraps to 0.37–0.41 s. In round 1, a preview with no taps at all did about the same.
- The time-pitch stage accounts for under 0.1 s (S1, S2).
- Prerolling a paused player does nothing (S4).
- The remaining 0.2–0.4 s was not found by any of the four.

**Options:**
- **(a)** Ship S3. The metering taps move after the effects, and the level meter has to learn their stamps, which arrive one buffer early (#335). This is a meter change of its own, and it halves the hold without clearing it.
- **(b)** Keep the hold.
- **(c)** Open a further investigation beyond these four, as its own issue, with S3 as its first data point. Candidates: `AVPlayerLooper` or a queue player, the audio mix's own render path, or an `AVSampleBufferAudioRenderer` pipeline.

**Recommendation:** (b) for now, and file (c) as its own issue. No option measured here removes the hold, and (a) costs a meter change for half of it.

# Handoff: documentation site theme (Boppa Llewyn redesign)

## Overview

This handoff moves the documentation site (`docs/site/`) from the old Boppa Llewyn theme to the new Boppa Llewyn design system. The old theme imitated a furniture workshop: Cormorant Garamond display type, IBM Plex, warm-ebony greys, a cream light look, a brass accent and 2/4/8 px "joinery" corners. The new system is the one the company website and every app's docs share:

- **Type:** Geist for text, Geist Mono for eyebrows, code, keys and versions. No serif anywhere.
- **Colour:** neutral greys, with the logo green as the one accent. The app icons and the company mark supply the rest of the colour.
- **Shape:** 6/10/16 px corners. Hairlines separate things; shadows are limited to a 1 px card shadow and the screenshot window.
- **Brand:** the company mark (three toy blocks) and the name in the header, with the product after it: **Boppa Llewyn / Frame Job**.

Decisions confirmed by the owner:

- The new Boppa Llewyn design system replaces the old theme everywhere.
- The company mark is the building-blocks mark (`assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg`).
- Body type is sans-serif; nothing is set in a serif.

Not yet confirmed: which palette ships. This handoff ships **Neutral Light** for the light look and **Neutral Dark** for the dark look, the pair the design system recommends. The system also has three alternates (Cream & Coral, Field Green, Monochrome). They're in `tokens.css` and switchable in the reference page, so the owner can compare. Changing the palette later means changing two blocks of `tokens.css` and nothing else.

## About the design files

`Docs Theme.html` is a **design reference in HTML**: a static mock of a content page and the splash page, not Starlight's markup. Recreate it in the existing Starlight theme files. Map each part by the tables below, and don't copy the mock's class names. Open it from this folder in a browser (it loads Geist from Google Fonts and the real screens and mark from `docs/site/src/assets/`). The bar at the top switches page, look and palette; `?theme=dark&page=splash&bare=1` does the same from the URL.

## Fidelity

**High fidelity** for colour, type, spacing, corners and borders, in both looks, at 1440 px and 390 px. The page structure doesn't change: the 280 px sidebar and 680 px prose column are the site's current widths, and the table of contents keeps Starlight's own width (224 px in the mock). The header grows from 60 to 64 px (`--sl-nav-height: 4rem`). Icons in the mock are simple stand-ins; keep Starlight's own icons.

## Fonts

- **Geist** (variable, weights 100 to 900) and **Geist Mono** (variable, 100 to 900), both under the SIL Open Font Licence 1.1. Take the `latin` and `latin-ext` WOFF2 subsets from Google Fonts, as the current faces were. Self-host them in `public/fonts/` as now, split by `unicode-range` in `font-face.css`.
- Replace `public/fonts/OFL.txt` with Geist's licence text (it names the Geist Project Authors). Delete every Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex file and rule; nothing uses them afterwards.
- Preload the two `latin` files, Geist and Geist Mono: the page's first screen has both (the header's version badge and the page eyebrow are mono).
- `--sl-font: var(--bl-font-sans)` and `--sl-font-mono: var(--bl-font-mono)`. The stacks in `tokens.css` fall back to the Mac's own San Francisco and SF Mono. Remove `--bl-font-display` and every rule that sets headings in it.

## The parts, in order down the page

**Header** (64 px). Solid `--bl-surface` with a `--bl-line` bottom border, no blur. Gaps of 24 px.

- **Lockup** (`SiteTitle.astro`): the blocks mark at 32 px, then **Boppa Llewyn** in Geist 600 17 / 24 px at −0.02em, a `/` in `--bl-ink-subtle` weight 400, the site title (**Frame Job**) in weight 500, and the version badge. Gap 8 px. The badge is mono 500 12 / 16 px, `--bl-ink-subtle`, padding 2 px 8 px, pill-shaped, drawn with an inset 1 px `--bl-line-strong` ring. Below 50rem the company name and the slash hide, leaving the mark, **Frame Job** and the badge. The lockup still links to the docs home.
- **Search** (desktop): a 260 × 36 px field on `--bl-surface-sunken` with a `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md`, the placeholder in `--bl-ink-subtle` 14 px, and the ⌘K keys as small `kbd` (20 px tall). Below 50rem it's a 36 px icon button.
- **Theme toggle and GitHub link**: 36 px square ghost buttons, `--bl-radius-md`, icon in `--bl-ink-muted`; hover `--bl-surface-sunken` with `--bl-ink`. The toggle keeps its two-state behaviour and its storage key.
- **Menu button** (below 50rem): the same 36 px ghost button, keeping the 44 px hit area the current CSS gives it.

**Sidebar** (280 px). Background `--bl-bg`, a `--bl-line` hairline on the right, padding 32 px 16 px 48 px 24 px.

- Group labels: `eyebrow`, `--bl-ink-subtle`, 8 px above the links, 28 px between groups.
- Links: 15 / 20 px, `--bl-ink-muted`, padding 6 px 10 px, `--bl-radius-sm`, 1 px apart. Hover: `--bl-surface-sunken`, `--bl-ink`. Current page: `--bl-accent-soft` background, `--bl-accent-ink` text, weight 550. Keep the existing guard so hover doesn't override the current item.

**Page opener** (`PageTitle.astro`, through CSS). The content column is 680 px (`--bl-prose-width`), 56 px from the header.

- Eyebrow: `eyebrow` in `--bl-accent-ink`, 12 px above the title. This is the page's one accent-coloured label.
- Title: `heading-1`.
- Description: `lede` in `--bl-ink-muted`, 16 px below the title.

**Body.** Paragraphs and lists 16 px apart; list items 6 px apart. Links are `--bl-accent-ink`, no underline until hover (1 px underline, 3 px offset). `h2` has 48 px above and 12 px below; `h3` 32 px above and 8 px below.

**AtAGlance** (`.fj-glance`). `--bl-surface`, a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md`, padding 16 px 20 px, 32 px above. A two-column grid (terms at their own width, 24 px gap, 10 px between rows). Terms are `eyebrow` in `--bl-ink-subtle`; values 15 / 24 px, menu paths bold, keys as `kbd`, tools as inline code at 13 px.

**Shot** (`.fj-shot`). The capture at up to half its pixel width, as now, with a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md` and `--bl-shadow-card`, 32 px above. The caption is 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-subtle`, centred, 10 px below.

- **New `frame` prop**: for a full-window capture (a `*.window` screen), `<Shot name="04-editor.window" frame alt="…" />` draws the capture in a window frame instead:
  - a 36 px title bar on `--bl-surface` with three 12 px dots in `--bl-line` (not traffic-light colours) and the window title centred in 13 px weight 500 `--bl-ink-subtle`;
  - `--bl-radius-lg`, no border, and `--bl-shadow-window`, the site's only large shadow.
- Use `frame` on the splash's editor window. Leave partial captures (sheets, inspectors) unframed.

**Steps** (Starlight's `<Steps>`). Each number sits in a 28 px square:

- `--bl-surface-sunken` fill, 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-sm`;
- the number in mono 500 13 px `--bl-ink`;
- a 1 px `--bl-line` connector down to the next square.

Text is indented 48 px, with 20 px between steps.

**Tables**. Full width, 15 / 22 px. Headers are `eyebrow` in `--bl-ink-subtle`, 10 px above a `--bl-line-strong` rule. Cells are padded 10 px 12 px 10 px 0, with a `--bl-line` rule under each row. Code in a cell doesn't wrap, as now.

**Asides** (`:::note`, `:::tip`, `:::caution`, `:::danger`). Each is the system's callout:

- a full-tint background, the icon, and the type's word as the title;
- no border and no left accent bar;
- `--bl-radius-md`, padding 16 px 20 px, 24 px above;
- a 20 px icon beside a 15 / 24 px title (weight 600) and a 15 / 24 px body in `--bl-ink-muted`.

Show Starlight's aside icon; the current CSS hides it. The colours come from the blue / purple / orange / red mapping above, `-low` for the background and `-high` for the icon and title. The title stays sentence case; drop the mono uppercase it has now.

**Code blocks** (Expressive Code). `styleOverrides`:

- `borderRadius: '10px'` and `borderColor: 'var(--sl-color-hairline-light)'`;
- the code background on `--bl-surface-sunken`;
- the frame's title bar on `--bl-surface`, with a `--bl-line` rule under it and its title in mono 500 12 / 16 px `--bl-ink-subtle`, not uppercase.

Keep the two syntax themes (`github-light`, `github-dark-default`) and `useStarlightUiThemeColors`. Inline code is mono at 0.875em on `--bl-surface-sunken`, `--bl-radius-sm`, padding 2 px 5 px.

**`kbd`**. 24 px tall, 6 px side padding, mono 500 13 px `--bl-ink`, on `--bl-surface` with a 1 px `--bl-line` border and a 2 px bottom edge, `--bl-radius-sm`. Use the same anywhere a key is shown, search included.

**Buttons** (`LinkButton`). 16 / 24 px weight 550, padding 12 px 20 px, `--bl-radius-md`.

- `primary`: `--bl-accent` with `--bl-on-accent` text; hover `--bl-accent-hover`.
- `secondary`: `--bl-surface` with `--bl-ink` text and a `--bl-line-strong` border; hover `--bl-surface-sunken`.
- `minimal`: `--bl-ink` text, 12 px side padding; hover `--bl-surface-sunken`.

**Cards and link cards**. `--bl-surface`, a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-lg`, `--bl-shadow-card`, padding 24 px, 24 px grid gap. The title is `heading-3`; the body is 15 / 22 px `--bl-ink-muted`. Hover strengthens the border to `--bl-line-strong`. A card's icon chip loses its box; the icon is `--bl-ink-subtle`.

**Pagination**. Two cards as above, padded 16 px 20 px, 16 px apart, 64 px above. The label (Previous, Next) is 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-subtle`; the title is `heading-3`.

**Footer meta** ("Edit page" and the like). 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-subtle`, under a `--bl-line` rule 32 px below the pagination. Not mono.

**Table of contents** (224 px). Its label is `eyebrow` `--bl-ink-subtle`, 12 px above the list. The list has a 1 px `--bl-line` rail. Links are 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-muted`, padded 5 px 0 5 px 12 px. The current link is `--bl-ink` weight 500, with a 2 px `--bl-accent` rail sitting over the hairline. The mobile ToC bar keeps its current behaviour, recoloured with the same tokens.

**Splash** (`template: splash`).

- **Hero band**: full viewport width on `--bl-band`, with text in `--bl-on-band`. One way to bleed past the content width is `box-shadow: 0 0 0 100vmax var(--bl-band); clip-path: inset(0 -100vmax)` on `.hero`.
  - Content stays in the 1120 px container (`--bl-content-width`), padded 96 px top and bottom (64 px and 16 px sides below 50rem).
  - Two columns, `1fr 192px`, 48 px apart. The Frame Job mark (the existing hero image) shows at 192 px, and above the text at 96 px below 50rem.
- **Hero text**: the eyebrow is `eyebrow` in `--bl-on-band` at 80% opacity; the title is `display`; the tagline is `lede` in `--bl-on-band` at 86% opacity, at most 34em wide, 24 px below the title; the actions sit 32 px below it, 12 px apart.
- **Below the hero**: 64 px down, the framed editor-window Shot at the full container width. Then the requirements paragraph in `--bl-ink-muted`, 680 px wide, 48 px below. Then "Start here" as an `h2` with a `--bl-line` rule and 64 px above it, and the link cards in two columns (one below 50rem).

**Focus**. One rule everywhere: `outline: 2px solid var(--bl-focus); outline-offset: 2px`. It replaces the current two-ring box shadow and holds 3:1 on every surface in both looks.

**Motion**. Colour, background and border transitions at 120 ms, nothing else. Keep the reduced-motion rule.

**Feature index** (`.fj-filter`, `.fj-features`). The filter box sits on `--bl-surface` with a `--bl-line` border and `--bl-radius-md`. Its input is on `--bl-bg` with a `--bl-line-strong` border and `--bl-radius-sm`, with a 14 px placeholder in `--bl-ink-subtle`. The count is mono 12 px `--bl-ink-subtle`. The table follows "Tables".

## Doctored's site

`boppa-llewyn.css` is shared rule for rule with Doctored's documentation site (`public-docs/src/styles/custom.css` in the Doctored repository), and its header says to change both together. This handoff covers Frame Job only. Port the finished file to Doctored in a change of its own; until then, the two sites look different. Doctored's lockup reads **Boppa Llewyn / Doctored** with the same mark.

## Out of scope

- Page content, the sidebar's order and labels, `src/data/features.json`, search behaviour and anything the docs proof reads. The only content edit is the `frame` prop on the splash's Shot.
- Shipping the alternate palettes or a palette switcher.
- The company website (boppallewyn.com), which has its own handoff.

## Checking it

- `pnpm build` in `docs/site/` (the last word: links, anchors and imports), `node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs src/content/docs/index.mdx`, and `python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py`.
- Look at the built site beside `Docs Theme.html`, in both looks, at 1440 px and 390 px. Check the splash, a page with every part (Split clips has steps, a table and AtAGlance), a page with each aside, and the feature index. Nothing should scroll sideways at 390 px.
- Search the built CSS for `Cormorant`, `IBM Plex`, `oklch(` and `--bl-brass`. None should remain.
